docs.title: User Flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[User clicks requirement link] --> B{JavaScript intercepts click}
    B --> C[Prevent default navigation]
    C --> D[Fetch URL with HEAD request]
    D --> E{Does file exist?}
    E -->|Yes - 200 OK| F[Navigate to page normally]
    E -->|No - 404| G[Show modal popup]
    G --> H[User reads message]
    H --> I{User closes modal}
    I -->|Click X| J[Hide modal]
    I -->|Click OK| J
    I -->|Click outside| J
    I -->|Press Escape| J
    J --> K[User stays on current page]

docs.title: Technical Flow
docs.text:
1. Page Load: JavaScript inserts modal HTML into DOM (hidden)
  2. Click Event: Event listener monitors all clicks on the page
  3. Link Detection: Checks if clicked element is a link to req-*.md
  4. File Check: Sends HEAD request to check if file exists
  5. Decision:
  6. File exists: Allow normal navigation
  7. File missing: Show modal popup
  8. Close Actions: Multiple ways to dismiss the modal

`;

    color: #your-color-here;
}

.req-modal-button-primary {
    background-color: #your-button-color;
}

docs.title: Change the Link Pattern
docs.text:
By default, the modal intercepts links matching req-*.md. To change this pattern, edit the JavaScript:

// Current pattern
if (!href || !href.match(/req-.*\.md$/)) return;

// Example: Match spec-*.md instead
if (!href || !href.match(/spec-.*\.md$/)) return;

// Example: Match multiple patterns
if (!href || !href.match(/(req|spec)-.*\.md$/)) return;

docs.title: Add Additional Close Button
docs.text:
To add a "Go Back" button alongside the OK button:

// In modalHTML
<div class="req-modal-footer">
    <button class="req-modal-button req-modal-button-secondary">Go Back</button>
    <button class="req-modal-button req-modal-button-primary">OK</button>
</div>

Then add event listener:

const backBtn = modal.querySelector('.req-modal-button-secondary');
backBtn.addEventListener('click', function() {
    hideModal();
    window.history.back();
});

docs.title: Local Testing
docs.text:
1. Start MkDocs server: 

    mkdocs serve

  2. Navigate to requirements page: 

    http://127.0.0.1:8000/requirements/requirements-index-example/

  3. Click on requirement links:

  4. Links to existing files → Normal navigation

  5. Links to missing files → Modal appears

  6. Test close methods:

  7. Click X button
  8. Click OK button
  9. Click outside modal
  10. Press Escape key

docs.title: Browser Console Testing
docs.text:
Open browser console (F12) and test the modal programmatically:

// Show modal
document.getElementById('req-not-available-modal').style.display = 'block';

// Hide modal
document.getElementById('req-not-available-modal').style.display = 'none';

docs.title: Test Different Screen Sizes
docs.text:
Use browser DevTools to test responsive design:

  • Desktop (1920x1080)
  • Tablet (768x1024)
  • Mobile (375x667)

docs.title: 1. Keep Modal Lightweight
docs.text:
The modal should load quickly and not impact page performance. Our implementation:

  • Uses vanilla JavaScript (no dependencies)
  • Minimal CSS (under 200 lines)
  • No external resources to load

docs.title: 2. Maintain Accessibility
docs.text:
• Keyboard navigation (Escape to close)
  • Focus management (modal content is focusable)
  • Semantic HTML structure
  • ARIA attributes (could be added for screen readers)

docs.title: 3. Provide Context
docs.text:
The modal message should:

  • Explain why the requirement isn't available
  • Suggest next steps
  • Link to helpful resources

docs.title: 4. Test Thoroughly
docs.text:
Before deploying:

  • Test on multiple browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
  • Test on mobile devices
  • Test with keyboard navigation
  • Test with screen readers (for accessibility)

docs.title: Modal Doesn't Appear
docs.text:

# Open browser console (F12)
# Look for JavaScript errors

Verify files are loaded: 

// In browser console
console.log('Modal script loaded');

docs.text:
The fetch() request might be failing. Check:

  • Network tab in DevTools
  • CORS settings
  • File paths are correct

docs.title: Styling Doesn't Match Theme
docs.text:
Make sure you're using MkDocs Material theme variables:

/* Use these variables */
var(--md-default-bg-color)
var(--md-default-fg-color)
var(--md-primary-fg-color)
var(--md-accent-fg-color)

docs.text:
Check event listeners are properly attached:

// Add console logs for debugging
closeBtn.addEventListener('click', function() {
    console.log('Close button clicked');
    hideModal();
});

docs.title: Finding Your Extra Python Processes
docs.text:
The lessons learned in this page were part of the troubleshooting process for learning how to built this site.

Sometimes you may start a process that never ends, even when your IDE closes. Linux has a similar system, but in Windows you can see what processes are running and make informed decisions about which ones to stop.

docs.title: The Problem: Identifying Running Python Processes
docs.text: When you have multiple Python processes running, you need to identify which ones are important (IDE tools) vs. which ones you want to stop (like a stuck development server).

docs.title: Command 1: List All Python Processes
docs.text:
Basic listing (shows only process names and IDs):

tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq python.exe"

Output example: 

Image Name                     PID Session Name        Session#    Mem Usage
========================= ======== ================ =========== ============
python.exe                   27776 Console                    1     45,632 K
python.exe                   65964 Console                    1     42,108 K
python.exe                   52860 Console                    1     38,944 K
python.exe                    2416 Console                    1     41,220 K

Problem: You can't tell which process is which! They all look the same.

docs.title: Command 2: Show What Each Process Is Actually Running
docs.text:
Advanced listing (shows full command line):

wmic process where "name='python.exe'" get CommandLine,ProcessId

Output example: 

CommandLine                                                                                                                                             ProcessId
"c:\Program Files\Python\Python314\python.exe" c:\Users\gradu\.vscode\extensions\ms-python.black-formatter-2025.2.0\bundled\tool\lsp_server.py --stdio  27776
"c:\Program Files\Python\Python314\python.exe" c:\Users\gradu\.vscode\extensions\ms-python.flake8-2025.2.0\bundled\tool\lsp_server.py                   65964
"c:\Program Files\Python\Python314\python.exe" c:\Users\gradu\.vscode\extensions\ms-python.pylint-2025.2.0\bundled\tool\lsp_server.py                   52860
"c:\Program Files\Python\Python314\python.exe" c:\Users\gradu\.vscode\extensions\ms-python.mypy-type-checker-2025.2.0\bundled\tool\lsp_server.py        2416

Now you can identify each process:

  • PID 27776: Black formatter (VS Code extension) ✅ Keep running
  • PID 65964: Flake8 linter (VS Code extension) ✅ Keep running
  • PID 52860: Pylint linter (VS Code extension) ✅ Keep running
  • PID 2416: Mypy type checker (VS Code extension) ✅ Keep running

docs.title: Command 3: Find Specific Processes
docs.text:
Search for a specific program (like MkDocs):

wmic process where "CommandLine like '%mkdocs%'" get CommandLine,ProcessId

This helps you find only the processes you're looking for, avoiding unnecessary noise.

docs.title: Critical Thinking: When to Kill Processes
docs.text:
❌ DON'T blindly kill all Python processes:

REM BAD - Kills everything, including IDE tools!
taskkill /F /IM python.exe

✅ DO investigate first, then selectively kill:

  1. Identify what each process is doing
  2. Decide which ones are safe to stop
  3. Kill selectively by PID:
taskkill /F /PID 12345

Or better yet, stop it gracefully in the terminal where you started it (Ctrl+C).

docs.title: Case Study: MkDocs Infinite Refresh Loop
The Problem
docs.text:
When running mkdocs serve with build hooks that modify watched files, you can get stuck in an infinite refresh loop:

  1. Hook runs during build → modifies a file in docs/
  2. MkDocs sees the file change → triggers rebuild
  3. Hook runs again → modifies file again
  4. Loop repeats forever! 🔄

docs.title: The Investigation
docs.text:
Step 1: Recognize the symptom - Browser page constantly refreshes - Terminal shows continuous rebuild messages - Changes don't settle

Step 2: Check your configuration

Look at mkdocs.yml for hooks:

hooks:
  - docs/hooks/priority_badges.py
  - docs/hooks/generate_req_index.py  # ⚠️ Generates files during build!

Root cause: The generate_req_index.py hook creates/modifies docs/requirements/req-index.md during every build, which triggers another build.

Step 3: Verify MkDocs is running

REM Search for MkDocs process
wmic process where "CommandLine like '%mkdocs%'" get CommandLine,ProcessId

If found, you know it's running and causing the loop.

docs.title: The Solution
docs.text:
Option 1: Stop auto-reload during development

mkdocs serve --no-livereload
  • Prevents automatic page refresh
  • Hooks still run on each manual build
  • You manually refresh browser to see changes

Option 2: Dirty builds (skip unchanged files)

mkdocs serve --dirty --no-livereload
  • Faster builds
  • Only rebuilds changed files
  • Best for rapid development

Option 3: Fix the hook (advanced)

Modify the hook to only write if content actually changed:

# Before writing
if new_content != old_content:
    file.write(new_content)  # Only write if different

This prevents unnecessary file modifications that trigger rebuilds.

docs.title: Lessons Learned
docs.text:
1. Investigate before acting - Don't kill all Python processes blindly
  2. Use detailed commands - wmic with CommandLine shows what's really running
  3. Understand the system - Know how MkDocs watches files and triggers rebuilds
  4. Choose the right tool - Use --no-livereload when hooks modify watched files
  5. Document solutions - Future you will thank present you! 📝
